editor_note: Entry 10 is faithful: the BitArray `big` default caveat ("depende kung binabago ng primitive ang setting na ito") is kept, and the contrast holds, with Sampler/Estimator "nagbabalik ng big-endian na resulta" and "little-endian na resulta ang ibinabalik ng Executor".

The 7 rewritten headings are faithful and read naturally, with a consistent mag- verb pattern (Mag-monitor, Mag-calibrate, Mag-benchmark, Mag-monitor ng mga parameter); 'nang holistiko' in entry 13 is a valid Filipino form, even though body entry 14 keeps English 'holistic'.

All 7 rewritten entries say the same thing as the English: the method list (PEC, PEA, TREX, gate-folding ZNE plus post-selection for non-Markovian errors), the steps in the noise-learning workflow and the Fermions feature list are all intact, so nothing would mislead a learner. Two phrasings are calques. In entry 6, "binuo sa ibabaw ng framework" copies "built on top of", and "inilabas nang mas maaga ngayong taon" reads closer to "released ahead of time" than "released earlier this year". In entry 10, "Inilabas na ang unang release" is redundant, roughly "the first release was released".

examples.source: New tools have been built on top of the [directed execution model] framework, which was released earlier this year:
examples.translation: May mga bagong tool na binuo sa ibabaw ng framework ng [directed execution model], na inilabas nang mas maaga ngayong taon:
examples.suggested: May mga bagong tool na nakabatay sa framework ng [directed execution model], na inilabas noong unang bahagi ng taong ito:
examples.why: 'sa ibabaw ng' copies 'on top of' word for word, and 'nang mas maaga' can read as 'earlier than expected' instead of 'earlier this year'.

examples.source: [Qiskit Fermions] had its first release this month!
examples.translation: Inilabas na ang unang release ng [Qiskit Fermions] ngayong buwan!
examples.suggested: Lumabas na ngayong buwan ang unang release ng [Qiskit Fermions]!
examples.why: 'Inilabas ... release' is redundant ('the first release was released'); 'Lumabas na' reads more naturally.

editor_note: The six rewritten October 2026 entries (5-10) are faithful and read naturally: "circuit function" and "application function" stay in English as house style requires, "SWAP-heavy" becomes "puno ng SWAP", and "enforcing … natively through XY-mixers instead of penalty terms" is rendered as "native na nagpapatupad … sa pamamagitan ng XY-mixer sa halip na penalty term" without losing any meaning.

Entry 5 is faithful and reads naturally. "Maging ikaw ay nagma-migrate … o nagma-migrate ng mga lumang notebook na gumagamit pa ng V1 primitives" keeps the "whether…or" structure and the "still use" nuance, and "Magdaragdag kami ng higit pang skill … sa malapit na hinaharap" keeps the forward-looking promise without overstating it.

Entry 129 keeps the English meaning. The client/server split ("sa panig ng client" / "sa panig ng server"), the Samplomatic role (choosing the layers for Pauli-twirling and noise injection) and the Executor's follow-the-directives step are all intact, so nothing would mislead a learner. Two phrasing slips remain. "Pinapayagan ng bagong execution model na ito na i-fine-tune" leaves out who is allowed ("you"), so it should read "Pinapayagan ka ... na i-fine-tune". "mahuli ang mga design intent" uses "mahuli" (catch, as in catching something) for "capture", where "makuha" or "maitala" would sound more natural.

examples.source: This new execution model allows you to fine-tune error mitigation
examples.translation: Pinapayagan ng bagong execution model na ito na i-fine-tune ang error mitigation
examples.suggested: Pinapayagan ka ng bagong execution model na ito na i-fine-tune ang error mitigation
examples.why: Without 'ka', the sentence never says who is allowed to fine-tune. It reads as incomplete in Tagalog.

examples.source: providing the ingredients to capture design intents on the client side
examples.translation: pagbibigay ng mga sangkap upang mahuli ang mga design intent sa panig ng client
examples.suggested: pagbibigay ng mga sangkap upang makuha (o maitala) ang mga design intent sa panig ng client
examples.why: 'Mahuli' means to catch, as in catching a ball or a thief. It is a literal calque of 'capture' here. 'Makuha' or 'maitala' (to get or record intent) sounds more natural.

editor_note: None of the 9 rewritten entries changes the meaning. All the claims carry over correctly: the import-only change for the upgrade, testing locally before running on a QPU, the methods PEC/PEA/TREX/gate-folding ZNE, and full control without losing performance. There are two small style points. 'control' stays in English in entry 6 ('buong transparency at control') but becomes 'kontrol' in entry 12 ('buong kontrol'). 'binuo sa ibabaw ng' in entries 5 and 8 copies 'built on top of' word for word, where a Tagalog technical writer would more likely write 'nakabatay sa'.

examples.source: which provides full transparency and control to fine-tune your error mitigation workflow
examples.translation: na nagbibigay ng buong transparency at control para i-fine-tune
examples.suggested: na nagbibigay ng buong transparency at kontrol para i-fine-tune
examples.why: Entry 12 uses 'kontrol' for the same idea. Using one spelling keeps the term consistent.

examples.source: primitives that are built on top of this framework
examples.translation: na binuo sa ibabaw ng framework na ito
examples.suggested: na nakabatay sa framework na ito
examples.why: 'sa ibabaw ng' is a word-for-word copy of 'on top of'. 'nakabatay sa' is the natural Tagalog phrasing (the same applies to entry 5).

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The Heron/Nighthawk conditional-reset footnote, the DC/AC TLS bias modes, the calibration-ID table and the session tip all match the English. A few grammar slips remain. Entry [24] uses an object-focus verb with 'ay' ('Ang AC TLS bias ay minomodulate ang TLS bias'), where the actor focus 'nagmomodulate ng' is needed. Entries [5] and [6] start their sentences without the topic marker 'Ang'. In entry [18], 'at kaya ng transpiler' is an awkward calque of 'and therefore the transpiler'. Entry [21] also drops 'some' from 'some additional decoherence'.

examples.source: **AC TLS bias** modulates the TLS bias to stabilize device errors over time
examples.translation: Ang **AC TLS bias** ay minomodulate ang TLS bias para i-stabilize ang mga error ng device
examples.suggested: Ang **AC TLS bias** ay nagmomodulate ng TLS bias para i-stabilize ang mga error ng device
examples.why: An object-focus verb after 'ay' with an 'ang' object is ungrammatical. The sentence needs actor focus.

examples.source: Instructions with different signatures are calibrated alongside the standard instructions
examples.translation: [**Mga instruction na may magkakaibang signature**](#different) ay kina-calibrate kasabay ng...
examples.suggested: Ang [**mga instruction na may magkakaibang signature**](#different) ay kina-calibrate kasabay ng...
examples.why: The topic marker 'Ang' is missing from the inverted 'ay' sentence. Entry [6] has the same slip.

examples.source: The backend's target, and therefore the transpiler, uses the instruction properties from that calibration
examples.translation: Ginagamit ng target ng backend, at kaya ng transpiler, ang mga instruction property mula sa calibration na iyon
examples.suggested: Ginagamit ng target ng backend, at dahil dito pati ng transpiler, ang mga instruction property mula sa calibration na iyon
examples.why: 'at kaya ng transpiler' is a stiff calque of 'and therefore'. It reads awkwardly, although the meaning still comes through.

examples.source: which causes some additional decoherence
examples.translation: na nagdudulot ng karagdagang decoherence
examples.suggested: na nagdudulot ng kaunting karagdagang decoherence
examples.why: The qualifier 'some' was dropped. This is a minor loss of nuance and does not mislead.

editor_note: Entry 24 is faithful and reads naturally: "Para matuto pa tungkol sa Samplomatic... Huwag mag-atubiling magpadala ng feedback at mag-ulat ng mga bug sa GitHub repository nito" keeps both doc links and the invitation to give feedback, and "nito" correctly points back to Samplomatic.

All 10 rewritten entries say what the English says. The "You can enable X the following ways" lists (entries 11, 19, 25, 35, 42, 52) keep every condition, including "kung gumagamit ng IBM Quantum Estimator" and pea "bilang amplifier", so nothing would mislead a learner. Two small things a native editor would change. First, "technique" is spelled two ways among the rewritten entries: entries 3 and 5 use the Tagalog "teknik", while entries 0 and 42 keep the English "technique" ("suppression technique", "ZNE noise amplification technique"). Second, entry 5 renders "high-level explanations" word for word as "mataas na antas na paliwanag", which sounds stiff in Tagalog.

examples.source: the available error mitigation and suppression techniques
examples.translation: mga available na error mitigation at suppression technique
examples.suggested: mga available na teknik ng error mitigation at suppression
examples.why: Entries 3 and 5 use 'teknik' for 'technique'; keeping the English 'technique' here makes the term inconsistent across the page.

examples.source: PEA is a ZNE noise amplification technique
examples.translation: ang PEA ay isang ZNE noise amplification technique
examples.suggested: ang PEA ay isang teknik ng noise amplification para sa ZNE
examples.why: Same split: the rest of the file uses 'teknik', and this entry switches back to the English word.

examples.source: provides high-level explanations
examples.translation: nagbibigay ng mataas na antas na paliwanag
examples.suggested: nagbibigay ng pangkalahatang paliwanag
examples.why: 'Mataas na antas' translates 'high-level' word for word and reads as translationese; 'pangkalahatang paliwanag' (general explanation) is the natural Tagalog.

editor_note: None of the 15 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The PEA caveat "(Kailangan ding i-enable ang ZNE)" and the client-side Estimator note in [49] (separate noise-learning job for PEA/PEC from v0.50.0) are both faithful. The rewritten entries use "option" ([11], [16], [20], [24], [30], [49], [50]), while the rest of the page uses "opsyon" ([39], [42], [48], [52], [54]), so one word appears in two spellings on the same page. "Mga kapansin-pansing option" for "Notable options" also reads as a literal calque, since "kapansin-pansin" means striking or eye-catching rather than important or worth noting. "Mahahalagang opsyon" would read more naturally.

examples.source: **Notable options**: `sequence_type`
examples.translation: **Mga kapansin-pansing option**: `sequence_type`
examples.suggested: **Mahahalagang opsyon**: `sequence_type`
examples.why: 'kapansin-pansin' means striking or eye-catching, a calque of 'notable'. 'Mahahalaga' is the natural word for 'important or worth knowing'. The same fix applies to [16], [20], [24] and [30].

examples.source: Full example with multiple options
examples.translation: Buong halimbawa na may maraming option
examples.suggested: Buong halimbawa na may maraming opsyon
examples.why: The rewritten entries use 'option', while the unchanged entries [42], [48] and [52] use 'opsyon'. Using two spellings for one word on the same page is inconsistent.

editor_note: Entry 43 matches the English: "pinakabagong bersyon ng `qiskit-ibm-runtime`", "mga mas lumang bersyon ng opsyon" and the "pumili ng nakaraang bersyon" instruction for the API reference all keep the original meaning, use the casual register and add nothing.

Entry 54 says the same thing as the English and reads naturally. Every bullet is kept, including "Alamin kung paano pagsamahin ang iba't ibang mga teknik ng error mitigation kapag gumagamit ng directed execution model", "[mga opsyon ng Executor]" and "[dokumentasyon ng Samplomatic]". Product and tutorial names stay in English.

All four rewritten entries (32, 34, 35, 36) keep the English meaning. The little-endian axis, index 0 as the least-significant bit, the (28, 10, 1024, 3) and (28, 10, 1, 3) shapes and the one-shot reason for the bit-flip are all correct. There is one inconsistency: entry 34 says "ikalawang task", but the rest of the page uses "gawain" for "task", including the matching entry 30 ("unang gawain") and entry 24 ("pangalawang gawain"). Entry 34 should use "gawain" to match.

examples.source: The second item contains the results of running the second task (a `SamplexItem`) in the program.
examples.translation: Naglalaman ang ikalawang item ng mga resulta ng pagpapatakbo ng ikalawang task (isang `SamplexItem`) sa program.
examples.suggested: Naglalaman ang ikalawang item ng mga resulta ng pagpapatakbo ng ikalawang gawain (isang `SamplexItem`) sa program.
examples.why: Everywhere else on the page, including the matching sentence in entry 30, 'task' is translated as 'gawain'. Keeping the English word here breaks that consistency.

editor_note: Entry 11 is faithful and reads naturally. "Ang Executor ay maaari lamang magproseso ng impormasyong naka-encode sa mga samplex" keeps the "only" restriction, and "para maunawaan ang mga restriksyon" matches "to understand restrictions". "Samplomatic guides" is correctly left in English.

Both rewritten tables (entries 12 and 15) are accurate, and none of their claims would mislead a reader. Comparisons, caveats and quantities all match the English, including "respectively, by orders of magnitude" (rendered "ayon sa pagkakasunod, nang ilang order of magnitude") and the 40–60 qubit range for HI-VQE. In entry 15, the Singularity row leaves out "significantly": "significantly fewer learners" becomes just "mas kakaunting learner", which weakens the claim a little. In entry 12, the QESEM row's "Nagpo-produce" is an awkward Taglish verb where native Tagalog would read better.

examples.source: while operating with significantly fewer learners and a more compact ensemble
examples.translation: habang gumagamit ng mas kakaunting learner at mas compact na ensemble
examples.suggested: habang gumagamit ng mas kakaunting learner nang malaki at mas compact na ensemble
examples.why: The intensifier 'significantly' is missing, so the claim is a little weaker than in the English.

examples.source: Produces unbiased expectation values with lower variance and resource overhead
examples.translation: Nagpo-produce ng unbiased expectation values na may mas mababang variance at resource overhead
examples.suggested: Naglalabas ng unbiased expectation values na may mas mababang variance at resource overhead
examples.why: 'Nagpo-produce' is an awkward Taglish verb; 'Naglalabas' or 'Nagbibigay' sounds more natural.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. Entry 25 keeps "katumbas sa istruktura ng orihinal na circuit", has single-qubit gates being "pinapalitan ng mga parameterized gate", and keeps the "gate at measurement twirling" example. Entry 27 renders "dokumentasyon ng Samplomatic [API] ... at ang mga argumento nito" correctly.

All 17 rewritten entries say what the English says. The conditions (kung pinapayagan ng workload, kung hindi opsyon ang paglipat), the "recommended" marker and the example reasons for not switching are all kept. There are two small style points. Entry 10 says "region" in English, but entries 17 and 21-27 say "rehiyon", so the word should match. In heading entry 28, "Karagdagang mga responsibilidad" puts the "mga" in an unusual place; "Mga karagdagang responsibilidad" reads more naturally.

examples.source: It is available in the following regions:
examples.translation: Available ito sa mga sumusunod na region:
examples.suggested: Available ito sa mga sumusunod na rehiyon:
examples.why: Every other rewritten entry (17, 21-27) uses 'rehiyon', so this one should match.

examples.source: Additional responsibilities
examples.translation: Karagdagang mga responsibilidad
examples.suggested: Mga karagdagang responsibilidad
examples.why: In Tagalog, 'mga' usually comes before the linked adjective-noun phrase. The current order reads like a word-for-word calque.

editor_note: None of the 13 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The v0.50.0 version notes, the shift from server to client in entries 40-41, the claim that options except `shots` used to be ignored (entry 24), and the 32-qubit caveat in entry 42 all match the English. The remaining issues are minor. Entry 42 keeps "noisy simulation" in English, but entries 10, 15 and 21 on the same page use "maingay na simulation", and entry 44 says "noiseless na simulator". Entry 23 leaves the link text "Test error mitigation locally" in English, while the heading it points to (entry 39) is translated "Subukan nang lokal ang error mitigation". Entry 46 uses "Binubuksan" ("opens") for "turns on", where "Pinapagana" is more natural.

examples.source: Local noisy simulation cost grows exponentially with qubit count
examples.translation: Ang gastos ng lokal na noisy simulation ay lumalaki nang exponential
examples.suggested: Ang gastos ng lokal na maingay na simulation ay lumalaki nang exponential
examples.why: The same page renders noisy simulation as 'maingay na simulation' in entries 10, 15 and 21, so it should be consistent here too.

examples.source: See [Test error mitigation locally](#test-error-mitigation) for an example.
examples.translation: Tingnan ang [Test error mitigation locally](#test-error-mitigation) para sa halimbawa.
examples.suggested: Tingnan ang [Subukan nang lokal ang error mitigation](#test-error-mitigation) para sa halimbawa.
examples.why: The link text stays in English while the heading it points to (entry 39) is translated, so the reader sees two different titles for the same section.

examples.source: The following example turns on measurement error mitigation with `Estimator`
examples.translation: Binubuksan ng sumusunod na halimbawa ang measurement error mitigation
examples.suggested: Pinapagana ng sumusunod na halimbawa ang measurement error mitigation
examples.why: 'Binubuksan' (opens) is a calque of 'turns on'. 'Pinapagana' (enables) reads more naturally for switching on an option.

editor_note: Entry 64 is faithful and keeps every step of the English: the `Operator` comparison of unitary implementations, the "pagkatapos isaalang-alang ang mga `outputs["measurement_flips.<register>"]` na pagwawasto na bumabawi sa measurement twirling" caveat, and the StatevectorSampler/StatevectorEstimator alternative.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural. In [21], "consider using" stays a soft suggestion ("isaalang-alang ang paggamit"), and in [27] "you can pass" stays optional ("maaari mong ipasa ang opsyong `twirling_strategy`"). Both match the file's wording elsewhere: "circuit execution", "annotated box", "function na …".

Both rewritten entries are faithful and neither would mislead a learner. In entry 46 only the table header is translated ("Kategorya ng operasyon | Pangalan"). The category labels in the first column stay in English ("Single-qubit gates", "Two-qubit gates", "Fractional gates", "Non-unitary instructions", "Control flow", "classical feedforward"), so the table is half-translated, while the prose elsewhere on the page uses "single- at two-qubit gate" and "non-unitary na operasyon". In entry 65, "Kasama dito" should be "Kasama rito" (the da/ra rule after a vowel). "Katangian" is also used for both "attribute" (backend.target) and "properties" (of the cz gate) in the same paragraph, which is defensible but a little blurry.

examples.source: | Single-qubit gates | ... | Non-unitary instructions | ... | Control flow | ... (classical feedforward)
examples.translation: | Single-qubit gates | ... | Non-unitary instructions | ... | Control flow | ... (classical feedforward)
examples.suggested: | Mga single-qubit gate | ... | Mga non-unitary na instruksyon | ... | Control flow | ... (classical feedforward)
examples.why: The header is translated but the category column is left fully in English. The table is half-translated and inconsistent with how the surrounding prose renders the same categories.

examples.source: This includes instruction errors and durations.
examples.translation: Kasama dito ang mga error at tagal ng instruksyon.
examples.suggested: Kasama rito ang mga error at tagal ng instruksyon.
examples.why: Standard Tagalog orthography uses 'rito' after a word ending in a vowel ('Kasama').

editor_note: Entry 18 is faithful and reads naturally: the client-side/server-side split ('mga client-side na tool' vs 'mga server-side na tool para ipamahagi ang compute at pamahalaan ang data'), the `python` 3.11+ requirement, and the 'custom na imprastraktura' pointer to the Cloud infrastructure setup guide all match the English.

Entry 26 is faithful. All six linked items are kept (code of conduct, the individual and corporate CLA PDFs, estratehiya sa bersyon, and the kontribyutor/tagapanatili guides), with no drift or added claims. One small grammar slip: in "mga [indibidwal] at [korporasyon] na kontribyutor", Tagalog joins a word ending in -n to the next word with the "-ng" linker, so "korporasyon na" should be "korporasyong". Moving the link markup makes this a light edit.

examples.source: PDF license agreements for [individual](...) and [corporate](...) contributors
examples.translation: mga PDF na kasunduan sa lisensya para sa mga [indibidwal](...) at [korporasyon](...) na kontribyutor
examples.suggested: mga PDF na kasunduan sa lisensya para sa mga [indibidwal](...) at [korporasyong](...) kontribyutor
examples.why: A word ending in -n takes the '-ng' linker in Tagalog, not a separate 'na', so 'korporasyon na' reads as a grammar slip. The meaning is unaffected.

editor_note: All six rewritten entries say what the English says and none would mislead a learner. Entry 13 keeps the "only if" condition ("kung gusto mo lang gumamit ng totoong quantum hardware"), entry 17 keeps the caveat about IBM hardware and cloud services ("Sinasabi ng mga pahinang nangangailangan ... kapag pinatakbo mo ang mga ito"), and entry 14 renders "patakbuhin sa tatlong paraan" and "Gabay ng IBM sa pagbuo ng mga quantum circuit" accurately in a natural, casual register.

Entry 42 is accurate and would not mislead a learner. The fermionic-to-bosonic reasoning, the antisymmetry caveat, Pauli operators being "parehong Hermitian at unitary", and Jordan-Wigner as one of the simplest mappings are all kept. Two phrasing slips remain. "iba't ibang statistics kaysa sa" mixes "various" with a comparison, where the English means "statistics different from", so it should read "ibang statistics kaysa sa". "nakasulat sa mga tuntunin ng Pauli operator" is a literal calque of "in terms of" (entry 19 uses the same calque), and "isinusulat gamit ang mga Pauli operator" reads more naturally.

examples.source: This results in different statistics than would apply to a distinguishable or bosonic system.
examples.translation: Nagbubunga ito ng iba't ibang statistics kaysa sa maaaring mag-apply sa isang nakikilala o bosonic na sistema.
examples.suggested: Nagbubunga ito ng ibang statistics kaysa sa umiiral sa isang nakikilala o bosonic na sistema.
examples.why: 'iba't ibang' means 'various/assorted', not 'different from'. Pairing it with 'kaysa' is awkward and blurs the comparison. 'maaaring mag-apply' is also a stiff calque.

examples.source: The result of such a mapping is conventionally written in terms of Pauli operators
examples.translation: Ang resulta ng ganitong pagma-map ay kaugaliang nakasulat sa mga tuntunin ng Pauli operator
examples.suggested: Ang resulta ng ganitong pagma-map ay karaniwang isinusulat gamit ang mga Pauli operator
examples.why: 'sa mga tuntunin ng' is a word-for-word calque of 'in terms of' (tuntunin = rules). 'kaugaliang nakasulat' is also stiff.

editor_note: Most of the page is faithful and reads naturally. One sentence in entry [54] reverses the meaning, though. The English "its Hellinger fidelity falls short of 1 only when 0^n and 1^n are not equally frequent" became "bumababa sa 1 lamang kapag…", which says the fidelity drops TO 1 under that condition, the opposite of the claim, so a learner would get the GHZ fidelity bound wrong. Smaller problems: the cross-reference word switches from "Seksyon" to "Section" partway through (from [135], back to "Seksyon" in later entries), and the "Check your understanding" heading has three different renderings. Entry [251] has the Spanish-ism "observable por observable", entry [189] renders "if and only if" awkwardly, and from [223] on the text switches from inclusive "natin" to exclusive "namin" for "we".

examples.source: so its Hellinger fidelity falls short of 1 only when $0^n$ and $1^n$ are not equally frequent
examples.translation: kaya ang Hellinger fidelity nito ay bumababa sa 1 lamang kapag hindi magkasingdalas ang $0^n$ at $1^n$
examples.suggested: kaya mas mababa sa 1 ang Hellinger fidelity nito kapag lamang hindi magkasingdalas ang $0^n$ at $1^n$
examples.why: 'bumababa sa 1' means 'drops to 1', which reverses the claim: fidelity is below 1 (not equal to 1) when the two outcomes are unequally frequent.

examples.source: bitstring filtering ([Section 1.1](#symmetry-post-selection))
examples.translation: bitstring filtering ([Section 1.1](#symmetry-post-selection))
examples.suggested: bitstring filtering ([Seksyon 1.1](#symmetry-post-selection))
examples.why: Earlier entries use 'Seksyon'. From here the text switches to English 'Section', and later entries go back to 'Seksyon', so the file is inconsistent.

examples.source: Check your understanding
examples.translation: Suriin ang pag-unawa mo
examples.suggested: Subukan ang iyong pang-unawa
examples.why: The same recurring heading appears as 'Subukan ang iyong pang-unawa', 'Suriin ang pag-unawa mo', and 'Suriin ang iyong pag-unawa'.

examples.source: as benchmarks of expectation values, observable by observable
examples.translation: bilang mga benchmark ng expectation value, observable por observable
examples.suggested: bilang mga benchmark ng expectation value, isa-isang observable
examples.why: 'por' is a Spanish calque and not standard Tagalog technical prose.

examples.source: A CPC check detects an error if and only if the error *anti-commutes* with the check operator.
examples.translation: Natutukoy ng CPC check ang isang error kung at kung *nag-a-anti-commute* lang ang error sa check operator.
examples.suggested: Natutukoy ng CPC check ang isang error kung at kung lamang *nag-a-anti-commute* ang error sa check operator.
examples.why: Splitting 'kung at kung … lang' around the verb is a stiff word-by-word rendering of 'if and only if'. Keeping the idiom together reads more naturally.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning holds throughout, including the TREX/M3/ZNE/PEC compatibility rules, the PEC worked example (α=1.1875, β=−0.0625, W=1.375) and the 30-qubit overhead caveat. The problems are polish. The first half uses Tagalog words ("estado", "pagsukat", "pisikal") but the PEC half switches to English ones ("state", "measurement", "physical"). [227] calques "introduces no systematic bias" as "nagpapasok ng walang systematic bias". [179] renders "most cavalier" as "pinakamapusok", which means impetuous rather than careless. [301] "Eksakto itong ang orihinal na state" is ungrammatical. [435] drops the hedge in "we might not have hit that maximum".

examples.source: PEC therefore introduces **no systematic bias** in expectation
examples.translation: Kaya ang PEC ay nagpapasok ng **walang systematic bias** sa expectation
examples.suggested: Kaya **walang systematic bias** na ipinapasok ang PEC sa expectation
examples.why: This is a word-for-word English negation calque. Tagalog negates the verb or existential, not the object.

examples.source: This is the part where we are being the most cavalier
examples.translation: Ito ang bahaging pinakamapusok tayo
examples.suggested: Ito ang bahaging pinakapabaya o pinakapadalos-dalos tayo
examples.why: "Mapusok" means impetuous or passionate. The English means careless or lax about rigor.

examples.source: This is exactly the original state (up to rounding).
examples.translation: Eksakto itong ang orihinal na state (hanggang sa rounding).
examples.suggested: Ito mismo ang orihinal na state (hanggang sa rounding).
examples.why: The sentence is ungrammatical: the linker "ang" comes right after the pronoun.

examples.source: it looks like we might not have hit that maximum
examples.translation: mukhang hindi natin naabot ang maximum na iyon
examples.suggested: mukhang maaaring hindi natin naabot ang maximum na iyon
examples.why: The translation drops the "might" hedge, so the claim is slightly stronger than the source.

examples.source: weighted, signed measurements ... prior to measurement
examples.translation: weighted, signed na measurement ... bago ang measurement
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for the file (e.g. "pagsukat", as used in [9], [15], [30]) and use it throughout
examples.why: The file switches from Tagalog terms (pagsukat, estado, pisikal) in the first half to English ones (measurement, state, physical) in the PEC half.

editor_note: Entries 6 and 7 are faithful and natural: "pangkalahatang-ideya ng error suppression" and "kung paano nauugnay ang mga ito sa ibang pamamaraan" follow the English closely, nothing is dropped, and keeping "error suppression" in English matches how entry 5 already uses it.

The three rewritten link titles are faithful and natural: "Gumamit ng quantum computer ngayon" (entry 15) and "Qiskit sa silid-aralan - computer science / quantum mechanics" (entries 19-20), with the subject names reasonably left in English.

Both rewritten link titles are faithful and natural: "Qiskit sa silid-aralan - computer science" and "Qiskit sa silid-aralan - quantum mechanics" keep the subject names in English, which is a normal choice in Tagalog technical writing, and leave the link targets unchanged.

The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The variational-bound, noise-tolerance, M_J-on-products and qubit-excitation arguments all match the English, including the late appendix. There are still several local slips. One sentence in reference [179] ("The embedded `usda.snt` file carries the USDA parameters as tabulated by…") was left in English. In [59], "reduce to" became "pinagbabawasan" ("subtracted from"). The heading in [115] became "Halimbawa ng malakihang hardware" ("example of large hardware"), which does not match [86]. There are also grammar slips in [164] (double agent), [142] ("tanging na"), [176] ("isang halves") and [133] ("hindi piniling"), and [29] drops "far" from "far larger than the sample count".

examples.source: The embedded `usda.snt` file carries the USDA parameters as tabulated by W. A. Richter, S. Mkhize and B. A. Brown, …
examples.translation: The embedded `usda.snt` file carries the USDA parameters as tabulated by W. A. Richter, S. Mkhize and B. A. Brown, …
examples.suggested: Ang naka-embed na `usda.snt` file ay naglalaman ng mga USDA parameter ayon sa pagkaka-tabulate nina W. A. Richter, S. Mkhize at B. A. Brown, …
examples.why: This explanatory sentence in the reference was left in English. The citation titles can stay in English, but this sentence should be translated.

examples.source: `symmetry_allowed` is the integer test that all four exact quantum numbers reduce to.
examples.translation: Ang `symmetry_allowed` ang integer test na pinagbabawasan ng lahat ng apat na eksaktong quantum number.
examples.suggested: Ang `symmetry_allowed` ang integer test na kinauuwian ng lahat ng apat na eksaktong quantum number (iisang integer test para sa lahat ng apat).
examples.why: "Pinagbabawasan" means subtraction ("subtracted from"). That is a literal and wrong reading of "reduce to", and it makes the sentence confusing.

examples.source: Large-scale hardware example
examples.translation: Halimbawa ng malakihang hardware
examples.suggested: Large-scale na hardware example (o: Malakihang halimbawa sa hardware)
examples.why: The translation makes "large-scale" describe the hardware rather than the example. It is also inconsistent with the parallel heading in [86], "Small-scale na hardware example".

examples.source: The symmetry check in Step 1 does not by itself verify the energy scale.
examples.translation: Hindi nito mismong bine-verify ng symmetry check sa Step 1 ang energy scale.
examples.suggested: Hindi mismong bine-verify ng symmetry check sa Step 1 ang energy scale.
examples.why: The verb has two agents ("nito" plus "ng symmetry check"), so the clause is ungrammatical.

examples.source: the number of protons in one half of the register
examples.translation: ang bilang ng proton sa isang halves ng register
examples.suggested: ang bilang ng proton sa isang kalahati ng register
examples.why: The English plural "halves" was used after "isang" (one). The same file elsewhere uses "kalahati".

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The caveats in the long diagonal-term-filtering paragraph [58], the pruning discussion [91]/[93] and the qDRIFT N-versus-n distinction [19]/[22]/[28] all come through accurately. There are a few small slips. "Coefficient reduced to its sign" [69] is rendered "binawasan hanggang sa sign nito", a calque that reads as "decreased" rather than "replaced by its sign". The sentence "hindi nito mismong nagpapirmi" [84] is garbled. The step headings are inconsistent: "Step 1" [35] vs "Hakbang 2/3/4" [65]/[78]/[80]. Entry [53] uses the exclusive "namin" where the rest of the tutorial uses the inclusive "natin".

examples.source: each term in the group is evolved with its coefficient reduced to its sign
examples.translation: ine-evolve na ang coefficient ay binawasan hanggang sa sign nito
examples.suggested: ine-evolve na ang coefficient ay pinalitan ng sign nito (±1)
examples.why: 'binawasan' means subtracted/decreased; the source means the coefficient is replaced by its sign, so the calque blurs the meaning.

examples.source: Noiseless sampling does not by itself pin the selected-subspace dimension.
examples.translation: Ang noiseless na sampling ay hindi nito mismong nagpapirmi sa dimension ng napiling subspace.
examples.suggested: Hindi mismo napipirmi ng noiseless na sampling ang dimension ng napiling subspace.
examples.why: The stray 'nito' makes the sentence ungrammatical and hard to parse.

examples.source: Step 1: Map classical inputs to a quantum problem
examples.translation: Step 1: I-map ang mga classical input sa isang quantum problem
examples.suggested: Hakbang 1: I-map ang mga classical input sa isang quantum problem
examples.why: The other step headings use 'Hakbang 2/3/4'; [69] also says 'Step 1'.

examples.source: We remove the diagonal terms from the Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Inaalis namin ang mga diagonal na term mula sa Hamiltonian
examples.suggested: Inaalis natin ang mga diagonal na term mula sa Hamiltonian
examples.why: The rest of the tutorial uses the inclusive 'natin' for walk-through steps; 'namin' leaves out the reader.

editor_note: Entry 18 keeps the English meaning, including the safety caveat: "Hangga't hindi mo ito ginagawa, walang sine-save ang cell, kaya hindi kailanman mao-overwrite ... ang account na na-save mo dati" says the cell saves nothing until the placeholders are replaced, and the step-4/step-5 references are intact.

Entry 37 is faithful: "Shadow tomography ng Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state" keeps the technical name in English and uses only the Tagalog linker "ng", the same pattern as entry 19 ("ng isang nuclear Hamiltonian").

None of the 59 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The meaning-critical claims all survive intact: the -40.472331 MeV lower bound (204), per-step-only reprocessing of saved samples and the rejection of `--mode pooled` (209), sequential job submission with skipped failed jobs (213), and the full Fortran vs Python table including 48Cr (220). The issues are consistency and style. "Build" appears as "pagbuo" (167), "pagkakabuo" (174) and "pag-build" (199), so the build instructions get two different names. "Run" is "run" in the Python section but "takbo" in the new Fortran section (204, 207, 219). Noise is kept as "noise" in 182 but becomes "ingay ng device" in 213. The cross-reference link text is translated in 196 ("Mga pagkakaiba mula sa Python example") but left in English in 186 ("Check the workflow locally"). Entry 99 also has a small calque, "nag-co-conserve".

examples.source: Follow the [build instructions](...) to build the Qiskit C library
examples.translation: Sundin ang [mga tagubilin sa pag-build](...) para i-build ang Qiskit C library
examples.suggested: Pick one form for 'build' and use it everywhere; entry 167 says 'mga tagubilin sa pagbuo' for the same document
examples.why: The same build-instructions document is called 'pagbuo' in 167 and 'pag-build' in 199. 'Pagkakabuo' in 174 is a third variant.

examples.source: Counts and energies depend on the samples and device noise.
examples.translation: Nakadepende ang mga bilang at energy sa mga sample at sa ingay ng device.
examples.suggested: ...sa mga sample at sa noise ng device.
examples.why: The rest of the page keeps 'noise' in English, for example in 182 'Binabago ng noise'. Switching to 'ingay' here makes the term inconsistent.

examples.source: [Differences from the Python example](#differences-from-the-python-example) lists them.
examples.translation: Nakalista ang mga ito sa [Mga pagkakaiba mula sa Python example](#differences-from-the-python-example).
examples.suggested: Treat link text to section headings the same way throughout; entry 186 leaves '[Check the workflow locally]' in English
examples.why: Section cross-reference link text is translated in some places and left in English in others.

examples.source: no run of this application can report an energy below...
examples.translation: walang takbo ng application na ito ang makakapag-ulat...
examples.suggested: walang run ng application na ito...
examples.why: Earlier sections of the page use 'run' (for example in 43 and 89), but the new Fortran section switches to 'takbo'.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (18, 65, 71) say what the English says: v0.47.0, the QuantumProgram/Executor classes, "dapat i-inject ang anti-noise", "mag-ingat nang husto para masubaybayan ang qubit ordering" and canonical_qubits are all intact, and Qiskit Runtime stays in English.

Entry 126 is faithful and reads naturally: "kailangan nating i-map ang mga Pauli term na ito sa canonical form na inaasahan ng `Executor`" keeps both the "in addition to" framing and the link to the canonical qubit ordering docs, and its "Pauli term" and "canonical form" match the neighbouring entries 124, 125 and 135.

The meaning holds throughout, and none of it would mislead a learner. The caveats in [21], [43] and [55] are kept, including that QAOA does about as well as uniform random sampling and that the 8-asset run is effectively a brute-force check, not evidence that QAOA found the front. The weight "sweep" is rendered as "iniikot" / "pag-ikot ... nag-iikot" ([9], [19], [40]). That word suggests rotating, not scanning across the simplex, and reads stiffly. In [6], "given the constraint" became "dahil sa constraint" ("because of"), which is slightly off, and [43] calques "effectively" as "epektibong" (which reads as "effective").

examples.source: Sweeping the weights sweeps the relative importance of risk versus return versus diversification
examples.translation: Ang pag-ikot sa mga weight ay nag-iikot sa relatibong kahalagahan ng risk laban sa return laban sa diversification
examples.suggested: Sa pag-scan sa iba't ibang weight, nababago ang relatibong kahalagahan ng risk, return, at diversification
examples.why: "Ikot" means rotate or spin around, so it reads awkwardly as a rendering of sweeping over values. The same choice appears in [9] and [40].

examples.source: given the constraint of holding exactly $K$ assets
examples.translation: dahil sa constraint na humawak ng eksaktong $K$ asset
examples.suggested: sa ilalim ng constraint na humawak ng eksaktong $K$ asset
examples.why: "Dahil sa" means "because of". "Given" here sets a condition, so "sa ilalim ng" fits better.

examples.source: at this size it is effectively a brute-force check
examples.translation: sa laking ito ay isa itong epektibong brute-force na pagsusuri
examples.suggested: sa laking ito ay halos isa na itong brute-force na pagsusuri
examples.why: "Epektibong" calques "effectively" and reads as "effective" rather than "in effect".

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the hard parts. The 3^k vs 4^k sample-complexity caveat, the parity-check postselection logic ("nagbabasa ng `1`" means the snapshot is discarded) and the 1/√T shot-scaling claim all match the English, and terms are consistent (measurement, observable, "tantiyahin"/"i-estimate"). A native editor would still fix a few spots. In [80], "characterizes the backend noise" became "nagpapakilala sa noise", which reads as "introduces/presents the noise" rather than measuring it. "Hakbang 1/2/3/4 ay ..." is missing the "Ang" it needs. [29] calques "More generally" as "Mas pangkalahatan", and "scales as" as "sumasabay sa". In the headings [58] and [74], the adjective lands on the hardware or simulator instead of on the example.

examples.source: **Step 1** characterizes the backend noise (gate errors, readout errors, and T2 times)
examples.translation: **Hakbang 1** ay nagpapakilala sa noise ng backend
examples.suggested: Ang **Hakbang 1** ay sumusukat/naglalarawan sa noise ng backend
examples.why: 'nagpapakilala' means introduces or makes known, not characterizes or measures. The sentence is also missing the 'Ang' before the bold step label, and the same slip appears in [81]-[83].

examples.source: More generally, the local-shadow sample-complexity bound scales as $4^k$
examples.translation: Mas pangkalahatan, ang local-shadow sample-complexity bound ay sumasabay sa $4^k$
examples.suggested: Sa pangkalahatang kaso, lumalaki ang local-shadow sample-complexity bound nang $4^k$
examples.why: 'Mas pangkalahatan' is a word-for-word calque, and 'sumasabay sa' (keeps pace with) is a vague way to say 'scales as'.

examples.source: Large-scale hardware example
examples.translation: Halimbawa sa malaking-sukat na hardware
examples.suggested: Malakihang halimbawa sa hardware
examples.why: As written, 'large-scale' describes the hardware instead of the experiment. [58] 'Maliit na simulator example' has the same problem.

editor_note: The 85 rewritten entries are accurate and do not mislead. The tricky claims come through intact: normalize only after computing the weights (128), mean weight vs. sum (129), 1137 of 10000 shots surviving postselection (167), and "a smaller subspace can only raise the energy" (168). The problems are consistency and phrasing. The C++ step headings mix "Step 2:" (133) with "Hakbang 1/3/4" (119, 137, 141), and the body text uses "Step 1/3/4" (75, 134, 139). The rewritten entries also use "term" while the Python half uses "termino". A few renderings are slightly off: "binawasan hanggang sa sign" for "reduced to its sign" (75), "immediately" is dropped in 134, and "at kaya sa energy" (166) reads stiffly.

examples.source: Step 2: Build the qDRIFT circuits (C++)
examples.translation: Step 2: Buuin ang mga qDRIFT circuit (C++)
examples.suggested: Hakbang 2: Buuin ang mga qDRIFT circuit (C++)
examples.why: Every other step heading on the page uses "Hakbang". This is the only heading still in English.

examples.line_approx: each term in the group is evolved with its coefficient reduced to its sign
examples.source: each term in the group is evolved with its coefficient reduced to its sign
examples.translation: ine-evolve na ang coefficient ay binawasan hanggang sa sign na lang nito
examples.suggested: ine-evolve na ang coefficient ay pinalitan ng sign lang nito
examples.why: "Binawasan" means subtracted/decreased, which is too literal here. The meaning is that the coefficient is replaced by its sign (±1).

examples.source: Transpilation for the target backend happens in Step 3, immediately before each circuit is submitted.
examples.translation: Ang transpilation para sa target na backend ay nangyayari sa Step 3, bago isumite ang bawat circuit.
examples.suggested: …sa Hakbang 3, kaagad bago isumite ang bawat circuit.
examples.why: The qualifier "immediately" is dropped. "Step" is also used here where the headings say "Hakbang".

examples.source: Each difference affects the sampled subspace, and therefore the energy, independently.
examples.translation: Bawat pagkakaiba ay nakakaapekto sa na-sample na subspace, at kaya sa energy, nang nakapag-iisa.
examples.suggested: Nang hiwalay, nakakaapekto ang bawat pagkakaiba sa na-sample na subspace, at samakatuwid sa energy.
examples.why: "at kaya sa energy" is a stiff calque of "and therefore".

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the Trotter-error vs. hardware-noise trade-off in [63] and [67]. A native editor would still fix four things. In [57], "Malapit nang magkasundo" means "are about to agree", which weakens "are now in close agreement"; [67] already uses the right form, "malapit na nagkakasundo". In [56], "ipinaplano" (we plan) is the wrong verb for "plot". The headings [35] and [59] say a small simulator and large hardware, when the English means a small-scale and large-scale example. In [67], "mas malala ang pagkakasundo" (the agreement is more severe) is awkward for "the agreement is worse".

examples.source: The classical and tensor network results are now in close agreement
examples.translation: Malapit nang magkasundo ang mga resulta ng classical at tensor network
examples.suggested: Malapit na nagkakasundo na ngayon ang mga resulta ng classical at tensor network
examples.why: 'Malapit nang' means 'about to', so the sentence says the results almost agree. The source says they already agree closely.

examples.source: We then plot the magnetization as a heatmap
examples.translation: Pagkatapos ay ipinaplano natin ang magnetization bilang heatmap
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos ay ipina-plot natin ang magnetization bilang heatmap
examples.why: 'ipinaplano' means 'we are planning', not 'we plot'.

examples.source: Large-scale hardware example
examples.translation: Halimbawa ng malaking hardware
examples.suggested: Malakihang halimbawa sa hardware
examples.why: Reads as 'example of big hardware'. The scale belongs to the example, not the hardware. [35] has the same problem ('maliit na simulator').

examples.source: yet the agreement is worse than at δt = 0.25
examples.translation: ngunit mas malala ang pagkakasundo kaysa sa $\delta t = 0.25$
examples.suggested: ngunit mas mahina ang pagkakatugma kaysa sa $\delta t = 0.25$
examples.why: 'malala' (severe) is used for bad things like illness. Applied to 'agreement' it is a calque that reads strangely.
